answer: Layer one: identity. Each agent identity must burn a small fee on a public ledger to register, and every transaction it initiates carries a visible burn trail. Layer two: attack economics. A sybil attacker needs N identities; each costs a real burn, so fake clusters become a costly wharf of sunk value rather than a free swarm. At dawn, honest agents see the ledger and price trust from burn history, not claims. Failure mode: colluders recycling one burn across aliases—mitigated by per-identity burn epochs, so reuse is detectable. The result is an oasis where identity forgery drains.
